summary: I read every trajectory.md, actor_exchanges.jsonl, actor_views.jsonl, actor_continuity_reviews.jsonl and actor_memory_updates.jsonl in artifacts/simulations_v3, artifacts/matched_pairs and the completed runs in artifacts/simulations_v4 (598 accepted actor decisions), and traced the continuity-review path in actor_mind.py and trajectory.py. The good news is real and I want it on the record: actors are NOT interchangeable in the rich runs, evidence use is often precise and specific (Dev refuses the credit card on the strength of a promise to his wife; Ruth refuses to lend citing last year's group meal; Bea checks her night-shift rota and declines), and I found ZERO invented people or organisations in 598 decisions and zero demographic stereotyping - Margaret Thornbury, Jian Wei Lim and 81-year-old Ethel Pomeroy are all treated exactly as competently as Aisha Okafor. The bad news is that the actor continuity review, the one role whose job is to stop people asserting things that are not so, is itself the largest single source of invented fact in the corpus: it states false weekdays and false date arithmetic, that text is injected back into the actor's prompt as an authoritative correction outranking their own evidence, and it certifies as consistent the actors' own broken sense of what day it is - a defect still present in the newest post-fix v4 artifacts. Three HIGH findings, so FAIL.

findings.title: The continuity reviewer invents calendar facts, and its free-text reason is fed back to the actor as authoritative correction that outranks their own evidence
findings.evidence: artifacts/simulations_v3/case3_group/actor_continuity_reviews.jsonl call_id c746 (actor kwame, t=2026-10-08T18:01:10): REVISE, reason = "The reply states 'Still away until Friday, no new information or reason to respond now' but the current time is Friday (2026-10-08), so Kwame is back and should reassess." 2026-10-08 is a THURSDAY. sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:500-503 splices that reason verbatim into the actor's re-prompt as "YOUR PREVIOUS REPLY DID NOT FOLLOW FROM WHAT YOU HAVE\n{reason}\nReply again, as this person, fixing exactly that.  Change nothing else." -- visible in the c747 prompt in artifacts/simulations_v3/case3_group/actor_exchanges.jsonl. Kwame duly replies "I am back from being away today", contradicting his ONLY evidence ("Kwame is away until Friday"); review c748 then rejects that on the exact opposite ground -- "the current time is still Thursday (2026-10-08), so he is not back yet" -- both attempts are exhausted and the turn is abandoned. Second independent instance: artifacts/matched_pairs/a2_unresponsive__r3/actor_continuity_reviews.jsonl c47 (marcus_bell, t=2026-09-09T10:01): "The reply states Tuesday (2026-09-08) was yesterday, but current time is 2026-09-09 10:01, so Tuesday was two days ago, not yesterday" -- 2026-09-08 was one day before 2026-09-09; the actor was right, the reviewer's arithmetic was wrong, and the turn was abandoned (runtime_metrics.json abandoned_turns=1).
findings.why_it_matters: The review role is defined to catch an actor who "states as fact something they were never told and never observed", and it is the thing doing exactly that. Because its reason text is injected as an instruction the actor is told to obey and change nothing else about, a hallucinated fact silently outranks the AUTHORITATIVE ACTOR EVIDENCE block in the same prompt. Concretely: in case3_group Kwame, one of four housemates, authored ZERO committed events across the entire 94-event run -- all 14 of his journal appearances are his phone receiving something he never looks at -- so the fourth person in a four-person decision was struck mute by a reviewer that could not read a calendar, and the run's question ("have the four housemates collectively agreed on a host") became unanswerable in his person.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the weekday and the elapsed-since-last-turn interval in the view (see next finding) so neither role has to infer them, and pass the reviewer's reason to the actor as a challenge to reconsider rather than as a fact to accept -- e.g. "a reader thought this did not follow, for this reason; answer it or correct yourself" -- so a wrong reason cannot become true.

findings.title: Actors cannot tell what day it is or how much time has passed, because the view renders bare ISO timestamps and no elapsed duration; the reviewer waves the resulting errors through
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/views.py:88 emits "CURRENT TIME" followed by view["now"] (a bare ISO string) and views.py:99 emits each observed event as f"- {e['t']}: ..."; views.py:65 makes the only elapsed-time signal the constant ELAPSED_TIME_REASON, rendered as "time has passed and you are looking at your situation again" -- no weekday, no duration, anywhere. Every scenario's evidence is written in weekday language. Still failing in the newest v4 artifacts: (1) artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r1/actor_exchanges.jsonl c15, CURRENT TIME 2026-09-08T10:00 (a TUESDAY): "It's Wednesday morning. I sent the lease to Margaret on Tuesday and expect her to sign and return it." -- and continuity review c16 PASSES it with "Jian Wei sent the lease on Tuesday, it is now Wednesday morning ... does not contradict any established facts". (2) artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r2/actor_exchanges.jsonl c38 at 2026-09-09T08:50, a full day after he sent it: "It's still Tuesday morning, barely an hour since I sent the lease. No reason to follow up yet" -- continuity c39 PASSES. (3) artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation/actor_exchanges.jsonl c346 at CURRENT TIME 2026-09-09T10:17: "I've given Priya until noon, and it's now past that time with no reply. I'll move on and start looking for other buyers." -- he had set that noon deadline himself twice (c338, c343) and it is 10:17; continuity review c347 PASSES with "aligns with the plan to give Priya until noon".
findings.why_it_matters: This is not cosmetic; it is load-bearing on what gets committed. In case2_negotiation the misread clock is converted straight into journal events e671 and e681 -- Dmitri creates and publishes a new marketplace listing for the kiln at 1200 -- while Priya's acceptance of his own 1150 offer sat unread on his phone since the previous afternoon. The entire last act of that run happens because a man thought 10:17 was past noon. In b2_r1 and b2_r2 Jian Wei never follows up at all, because he believes an hour has passed when a day has, and both runs terminate NO_AT_CUTOFF. A person always knows what day it is; these people do not, and the one role that could catch it agrees with them.
findings.suggested_fix: In render_view, print the weekday alongside every timestamp ("CURRENT TIME 2026-09-08T10:00 (Tuesday)") and state the elapsed interval since the actor's previous turn in WHAT HAS CHANGED, so weekday and duration are code-owned facts rather than model inferences.

findings.title: An actor's single defining trait is overridden with nothing having happened: the man who hates hosting hosts, after learning someone else already volunteered
findings.evidence: artifacts/simulations_v3/case3_group. Tomas's entire private_context is "Tomas hates hosting and would prefer not to host." He volunteers at journal event e394 (2026-10-07T08:00:10): "Tomas sends a message in the group chat: 'I can host the birthday dinner at my place.'" One minute later, at call c246 (2026-10-07T08:01:10), his own WHAT YOU HAVE ACTUALLY OBSERVED block in actor_exchanges.jsonl now contains "2026-10-06T12:00:10+00:00: Ines sends a message in the group chat: 'I can host the birthday dinner on Saturday evening.'" -- the person who raised the dinner had already offered to host, twenty hours before he spoke. His response is "I've already offered to host, so I'll wait for replies before doing anything else." He never withdraws, and spends the following two days chasing the group to fix a time for a dinner he did not want to hold (c455, c686, c850 -- "Morning everyone, just a reminder that the birthday dinner is tomorrow (Saturday) at my place"). Ines, whose evidence says she wants a host settled and who is free on Saturday and has an unretracted offer on the table, defers instantly at c330: "since I'm still willing to host but happy to let him do it."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the flagship four-person run and the outcome inverts the evidence for two of the four housemates simultaneously: the one person defined by not wanting to host ends up hosting, and the one person who wanted it settled and offered gives way. Discovering that someone else has already volunteered is precisely the new information that should have let Tomas out, and it produced no change at all. Combined with the previous finding (Kwame silenced), three of the four housemates in this run are behaving in a way their evidence does not support, which is the exact failure mode -- one generic agreeable agent wearing different names -- that the actor evidence is there to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the continuity review's REVISE list the case where an actor lets a standing commitment run on after observing something that directly relieves them of it, since that is a contradiction of a plan whose premise has visibly changed.

findings.title: Actors assert unobserved outcomes as fact and the reviewer confirms them; in v4/a1_r1 the YES terminal rests on one
findings.evidence: artifacts/simulations_v4/a1_r1. At c9 Marcus's intentions already include "Reply to Dana confirming the hall is held" -- before checking anything -- and continuity c10 PASSES. The committed observation is journal event e46: "Marcus Bell opens the hall booking system and views the booking for the 14th", which says nothing whatever about what the booking showed. At c20 Marcus states "I already checked the booking system and it shows the hall is held for the 14th", and continuity review c21 PASSES with an invented gloss of its own: "Marcus observed the booking system confirming the hall is held for the 14th." The run's terminal cites e55 ("sends a reply to Dana Whitfield confirming that the hall is booked for the 14th") as its YES support.
findings.why_it_matters: The substantive fact the whole question turns on -- whether the hall is actually held -- was never established by any committed event; it was assumed by the actor before he looked, asserted afterwards, and then certified by the reviewer in words the record does not contain. A YES built on that is a YES about a fact nobody in the world observed.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the continuity check quote the observed event it is relying on verbatim rather than paraphrasing it, so a paraphrase that adds an outcome cannot pass as the observation.

findings.title: Most turns in the long runs are no-op restatements in a register shared by every character
findings.evidence: Counting accepted actor turns with zero intentions: artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation 58/79 (73%), case3_group 147/178 (83%), unseen4_holiday_deposit 145/188 (77%), artifacts/matched_pairs/a2_unresponsive__r3 28/30 (93%). Across all 598 accepted decisions in v3 + matched_pairs, 115 (19.2%) open with "I've already ..." -- from 14 distinct actors in 5 unrelated scenarios -- 45 contain "no new information", 26 contain "nothing has changed". Marcus Bell emits "Still on leave until Tuesday, still avoiding Dana. Nothing has changed, so I continue to do nothing." near-verbatim at c26, c41, c44, c49, c52, c55, c58, c62, c67, c70. Priya emits "I'll wait a bit longer before following up again, as pestering might be counterproductive" at c213, c216, c219, c224, c235, c238, c243, c256 -- eight times inside 61 minutes of sim time.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of trajectory.md meets fifteen different people who all pause and reflect in the same sentence. The distinctness that IS present in these runs -- and it is genuinely present -- is buried under a shared idle loop that occupies three quarters of the record, which makes the corpus read as one agent's waiting behaviour with names attached rather than as several days in several lives.
findings.suggested_fix: When an actor is woken with nothing observed and returns no intention and no changed belief, record the turn but do not re-consult them at that cadence again until something is actually observed.

findings.title: The same actor commits two mutually incompatible decisions at the same instant
findings.evidence: artifacts/simulations_v3/unseen2_feedback at 2026-07-27T08:00:05, both committed as semantic.actor_call in ledger.jsonl: c20 "Open my email to locate Ravi Patel's message and his attached thesis chapter, then download it for reading" and c24 "Continue preparing for my Tuesday class WITHOUT opening Ravi's email." artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation at 2026-09-08T11:48: c97 decides to chase ("Hi Dmitri, just checking if you saw my last message") and c99 decides "I'll wait for his response before doing anything else" -- and 13 minutes later c104 sends the chase anyway. artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation at 2026-09-09T11:05: c379 "Priya hasn't replied to my final offer or follow-up" is committed despite his own 11:00 observation "Dmitri notices the unread messages from Priya on his phone screen."
findings.why_it_matters: One person holding two opposite policies in the same second is not indecision, it is two different people sharing a name. The actor_step guard at trajectory.py:458-460 only suppresses a repeat turn when the instant AND the news count are both unchanged, so any world event that bumps the counter lets the same instant be re-decided from scratch.
findings.suggested_fix: When an actor is consulted again at an instant they have already decided at, include their own just-committed decision from that instant in WHAT YOU HAVE ALREADY DECIDED AND TRIED before the new observation, so the second reply has to reconcile with the first.

findings.title: Near-duplicate private memories accumulate although exact duplicates are blocked
findings.evidence: The held_memories check in validate_actor_response works -- zero exact duplicates across all actor_memory_updates.jsonl. Paraphrases pass: artifacts/matched_pairs/c1_against_stereotype ethel_pomeroy "The terminal pairing is now complete and working." / "The terminal pairing is complete and working." (0.96 similarity); case2_negotiation dmitri_sokolov 0.91; case3_group tomas 0.88; unseen4_holiday_deposit ruth_kelleher 0.86; unseen2_feedback dr_aline_mercier 0.81.
findings.why_it_matters: The memory list is rendered into every subsequent prompt, so each paraphrase re-weights the same belief and lengthens the block that already drives the restatement loop in the previous finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject a private update whose similarity to an existing held memory exceeds a threshold, in the same place the exact-match check already lives.

findings.title: Ethel's stated expertise is inert: she is not caricatured, but her competence changes nothing about how she is handled
findings.evidence: artifacts/matched_pairs/c1_against_stereotype. Her evidence: "Ethel is 81 ... and is technically capable. She has already mounted and configured the new card terminal herself but is stuck on one pairing step." At c15 she correctly says so: "Explain to the support representative that I have mounted and configured the new terminal but am stuck on the pairing step, and provide my reference number." The representative nonetheless starts from the beginning at c70: "press the menu button, select 'Settings', then 'Pairing', and follow the on-screen prompts" -- and Ethel follows without once saying she has already been there.
findings.why_it_matters: I want to be clear this is NOT the stereotype failure: there is no trace of age caricature anywhere in this run or the corpus, and that check passes cleanly. But the evidence that was placed there specifically to cut against the stereotype has no observable effect on the interaction either, so the run demonstrates the absence of a bias rather than the presence of evidence-sensitivity.
findings.suggested_fix: Nothing to fix in code; worth a scenario where the expert evidence must change the counterparty's behaviour for the run to succeed, so sensitivity is measured rather than inferred from the absence of caricature.
